sentiment.instructions: Judge the feeling the tweet's author conveys (about events, people, plans, products), not the topic. Use positive or negative when there is a clear emotional or evaluative cue, even a calm one; otherwise neutral.

criteria.positive: Excitement, enjoyment, praise, love, hope or gratitude, loud or calm: 'can't wait', 'hyped', 'love', 'best', 'perfect night', 'for sure going to', 'congrats', 'good luck', 'I hope', ':)'. Festive or hype promos and eager self-promotion ('come celebrate', free treats, ticket giveaways, 'get your tickets now', 'come support', 'please share!!!'). Reports of a title, reaching a final, a championship or a historic moment. Sympathy, prayers, RIP wishes. Upbeat teasing.
criteria.neutral: Facts, headlines (including ones merely reporting criticism, reputation, controversy or opinion), schedules, ads, spam, dry event or info-session notices. Live score updates and routine match results, even with '!'. Casual plans ('X is the move tomorrow') and 'now watching' status. Questions, trivia, speculation, meme jokes. Pleas, wishes or requests to celebrities and fan campaigns, even with '!!!' or '<3'. Wry sports or TV banter ('implode', 'could be worse'). Hedged comparisons of politicians. Self-deprecating questions ('why did I just...'). Apologetic updates and minor mishaps told matter-of-factly or laughingly ('sorry for the lack of...', 'lmao', 'I'm dead' as laughter). Fan overwhelm ('not ready for this album'). Truly mixed opinions. Choose neutral when no clear cue exists.
criteria.negative: Anger, disappointment, sadness, frustration, dread, contempt or hostility: 'WTF', 'sucks', 'hate', 'worst', 'disappointed', 'I miss', ':(' or ':-/' complaints. Dread about tasks ('going to die', 'not in the state of mind'). Insults, profanity aimed at someone, contemptuous sarcasm or mockery, hostile rhetorical questions about people, politics or religion. Headlines about harm: attacks, missiles, bombings, deaths, funerals, injuries, crime charges, deficits, product defects or warnings ('may break').
